upcoming.title: Thursday Tastings
upcoming.body:
Every Thursday we host a free tasting from 5 to 7pm! These tastings feature a winemaker, winery, or a theme! Learn a little about wine and expand your palate with wines you won’t find on The Scout shelves. Each week is a different winery, and here are some of the upcoming featured wineries:

September 10: 15 Mile Winery

September 17: Domaine Divio (also this is Third Thursday in downtown Gresham!)

September 24: Familia Torres

October 22: Fayetta Vineyard

November 26 & 27: Closed for Thanksgiving

December 3: Meliora Wine

seoData.seoDescription: Every Thursday we feature a winemaker, winery, or region for a free tasting from 5 to 7pm! At The Scout in downtown Gresham, Ore.

upcoming.title: Live Music: Spiced Rye
upcoming.body:
Larry and Re Hart created Spiced Rye in 2018, after relocating to the Pacific NW, from the Central Coast of California, where they were founding members of the band “3 for the Road.” Leaving a bandmate behind, Larry and Re found themselves needing to reinvent their sound, as a duo. Re’s unique vocals have been described, by many, as having a tone that reminds people of Stevie Nicks, Tracy Chapman, Joni Mitchell, and Margo Timmins, as well as many others. Along with lead vocals, Re plays rhythm guitar, while Larry plays rhythm and lead.

Learn more about Spiced Rye HERE.

All ages welcome.

upcoming.title: Live Music: folkefire
upcoming.body:
Mike Phillips moved to Oregon in 2005 to explore its music scene and follow in the footsteps of his favorite artist at the time, Elliott Smith. Between 2006 and 2007 he joined a band with a popular run that included winning a Battle of the Bands at the Crystal Ballroom; releasing a single via Starbucks’ Hear Music record label; opening for acclaimed artists including Everclear and Seven Mary Three; touring 36 states —and immediately breaking up upon their return. Hailing back to a 90s-era PNW-style singer-songwriter tradition, he’s since turned his musical interests to pseudo-folk originals with an international flavor, storytelling, and Irish folk music specifically. In 2024 he moved to Gresham; folkefire is the latest incantation of his musical and personal interests.

Learn more about folkefire HERE.

All ages welcome.

upcoming.title: Live Music: Linda Daiber & Gene De Nardo Jazz Duo
upcoming.body:
Linda and Gene first crossed paths at a Hawthorne Boulevard jam session in 2006. Over the nearly two decades since, they’ve enjoyed a fun musical journey, performing in everything from intimate duos to swinging quartets and building a great community of friends and fellow musicians along the way. Inspired by an appreciation for a wide variety of jazz standards, Linda and Gene play to share the pure joy of music. They look forward to seeing you at The Scout Wine Bar!

All ages welcome.

upcoming.body:
Portland, Oregon based guitarist, synth wizard, and cinematic expressionist Alex Callenberger creates soundscapes to dream and swim through. Calling on the powers of electric guitar, live looping, electronic and experimental instruments, he casts sonic spells that straddle and bind the genres of ambient, down-tempo, experimental, psych, and folk-minimalism.

upcoming.title: Live Music: Dalton Huxley
upcoming.body:

Whether he’s playing with the band Winchester (@winchestertheband) or playing solo, you’re sure to hear something you’ll love from his wide selection of covers ranging from The Eagles to Chris Stapleton to Harry Styles and more!

Learn more about Dalton HERE.

Find him on Instagram HERE.

upcoming.title: Live Music: Cynthia Rae & Bobby Keys
upcoming.body:
Cynthia Rae is a band leader and vocalist who loves to connect with audiences through music. Her love of jazz is evident in her treatment of famous standards in a small group or a big band setting, and she brings a joyful rhythmic vibe to the music with her flute solos and auxiliary percussion.

Bob Jacobs has been playing keyboards practically his entire life.  He studied at Berklee College of Music in Boston, and has performed with a variety of musicians in the U.S. and Costa Rica, playing styles including blues, rock, salsa, cumbia, and primarily jazz.  He also produced and recorded two albums as primary composer of the jazz fusion band “Better Than Street Racket.”  He’s excited to be performing with Cynthia in the classic jazz vocal/piano genre.

All ages welcome.

upcoming.title: Live Music: Robert Meade
upcoming.body:
Robert Meade is a past performer of the Sundance Film Festival and a singer/songwriter, solo acoustic musician who has been entertaining Northwest audiences for almost two decades.  His brand of upbeat Americana, Rhythm 'n' Blues originals & classics of the 60s to 90s are bound to lift the spirit! With influences by Tom Petty, Bob Dylan, The Beatles, Neil Young, and Keith Richards of The Rolling Stones, you'll be transported back—or be introduced—to some of the greatest singer/songwriters of all time.

Find Robert on Instagram HERE.

Photo credit: Tatie B. Photography.

All ages welcome.

past.title: Live Music: Jackson Warner
past.body:
Born and raised in Oregon, Jackson Warner grew up on a steady diet of Tom Petty, Bruce Springsteen, and of course, Jackson Browne. Whether he knew it or not, those legends were laying the foundation in his heart and soul for a lifelong relationship with music.

Given his first guitar at age eleven, he began writing songs as soon as he learned three chords. Though he started at a young age, it took decades before he decided to share his songs with the world.

His debut EP, The Scenic Route, is the culmination of a life spent soaking up all the joys and pitfalls this world has to offer, and taking those often hard-learned lessons and putting them into song. Come to the show and come along for the ride.

Learn more HERE.

All ages welcome.

past.title: Live Music: RJ Bloke
past.body:
RJ Bloke is new to Portland, having recently relocated from Los Angeles,
where he was a well established songwriter, solo performer and
bandleader for Patrolled By Radar, in the Americana Roots Rock,
Alt-Country scene. In the folk-blues tradition of acoustic guitar and harmonica,
he performs originals with memorable melodic hooks and thought provoking
poetic lyrics, as well as reinterpreted choice cover songs. He has toured
the US extensively, both solo, and with his band.

He has recorded several independent full length albums, as well as
releases for Knitting Factory Records (Brooklyn, NY), and
Nomad Eel Records (San Pedro, CA). His songs have
been featured in numerous film and TV productions, including
"Shameless" (HBO), and most recently "Breakwater" (Hulu).

All ages welcome.

Music ranging from Thelonious Monk, to Joe Henderson, to Stevie Wonder, to Claude Debussy may appear in a single night.

past.title: Live Music: Lexie
past.body:
Lexie is a Portland based singer-songwriter, filmmaker, and actor. Her debut album, Halcyon Days, emerges on the heels of her completing chemotherapy, radiation, and surgery to remove a sarcoma tumor from her thigh. During five months of chemo, Lexie could not listen to music. Once in recovery, listening to pop music especially had a revelatory effect.

Timeless, vibrant, earthy, and sexy, Halcyon Days is a deeply personal account of Lexie’s recent life experience, offered through memorable hooks and a lush sonic landscape, thanks in large part to producer Alex Callenberger. With a voice to soothe, Lexie sings of desire, love, loss and ultimately the celebration of being alive.

Halcyon Days is due for release in the summer of 2026.

Find out more HERE.

All ages welcome.

past.title: Live Music: The return of edad del pavo
past.body:
edad del pavo is an acoustic instrumental project blending the intricate sounds of Spanish guitar with the rhythmic energy of Latin American percussion, all filtered through the introspective lens of Pacific Northwest indie rock and folk. Founded in Barcelona in 2016, the project has since moved to Gresham, Ore., where it continues to craft dynamic, atmospheric compositions that transport listeners across borders and genres.

Learn more about edad del pavo HERE.

Find it on Instagram HERE.

All ages welcome!

past.title: Live Music: 1,000 Fuegos
past.body:
Compositions painting an afro-cuban face with a transplanted american smile, 1,000 Fuegos presents eclectic sounds filtered by a modern pop perspective and spiced with colors of jazz. All the way from Hialeah, Fla.—a concrete melting pot of mostly Caribbean, Latin America, and US cultures—this music is a captivating challenge to conventional musical themes.

All ages welcome.

past.body:

All ages welcome.

past.title: Live Music: gardentender
past.body:
gardentender is the songwriting duo of Kyle and Linoy — partners in life and music. Their songs, written together, are rooted in harmony and connection, weaving stories of love, growth, and quiet resilience. With a sound that draws from folk, indie, and Americana, gardentender offers a set that’s tender, textured, and deeply human. Their song “Happy Song” was a runner-up in the Portland Folk Fest 2026 Song Contest.

Learn more about gardentender HERE.

Find them on Instagram HERE.

Photo credit: @alacrityphotography.

All ages welcome.

past.title: Live Music: The AM (Acoustic Minds)
past.body:
Acoustic Minds is a Portland-born, twin-fronted project led by identical sisters Jenni and Amanda Price—built on connection, instinct, and a shared pulse you can feel from the first note. They’ve been singing together their entire lives. Not learned—lived. That connection is the foundation of everything: the way they blend, the way they move, the way they build energy without ever needing to say it out loud.

What started as two voices has grown into something bigger. Alongside longtime collaborators Aaron Altemose and Josh Lorenzen (SubCo), Acoustic Minds has evolved into a full, immersive sound—layering lush harmonies with bass-driven grooves, modern production, and textured electronic elements.

The result lives in the in-between:

‍dreamy but grounded,
emotional but dancy,
polished but still raw where it matters.

Learn more about The AM HERE.

All ages welcome.

past.title: Artist Talk: Cameron Holly Dexter
past.body:
Join visual artist and film producer Cameron Holly Dexter for an intimate artist talk celebrating her current in-shop residency. Cameron will share the stories behind her surreal art practice, discussing how she uses vintage imagery and celestial elements to explore women's internal landscapes.

She will also speak on how her studio art connects with her film career, exploring her background in visual storytelling across both mediums. Grab a glass of wine and join us for an evening of art, storytelling, and community conversation!

All ages welcome.

past.title: Live Music: Bronwen Roberts
past.body:
Bronwen Roberts is a Portland-based singer-songwriter, guitarist, and recording artist, specializing in unconventional rhythms and fingerpicking techniques. Fluent in four languages, her repertoire spans Brazilian jazz, French YéYé, Americana, and other world music — as well as her own alt-folk compositions.

Originally from Texas, she attended college at Yale University and the University of Paris, later moving to Rio de Janeiro where she studied Brazilian rhythms. Her studio albums Breathless (2025) and False Start (2017) evoke the stripped-down, acoustic styles of Nick Drake, Caetano Veloso, and Joni Mitchell. She is currently involved in a number of Portland-area music projects, including her psych-folk band Revelever.

Learn more about Bronwen HERE.

Find her on Instagram HERE.

All ages welcome.

past.title: Live Music: Morning Breath
past.body:
Meet Luke + Molly: video editors by day, Morning Breath by night. Sweethearts in real life, they are both songwriters and multi-instrumentalists. Pairing irreverently heartfelt lyrics with mellifluous vocal harmonies, their brand of scrappy folk-pop will worm its way into your heart and insulate your insides against the bitter chill of rain-drenched Pacific Northwest evenings.

Based in Portland, Ore., they began playing in the spring of 2025, and have already performed in a variety of venues including a tree-squatter’s platform, a WPA-era concrete tunnel, and their own backyard.

This Should Be Illegal—out on February 27—is their debut album. Aside from Luke and Molly, the Morning Breath touring band is rounded out with the absurd talents of Matt Harmon, Kali Giaritta, Cole Huiskamp, and Steve Foster.

Find them on Instagram HERE.

All ages welcome.

past.title: Live Music: Maggie Ray
past.body:
Maggie Ray is a Portland-based folk-pop acoustic artist with a wide-ranging sound, from intimate singer-songwriter ballads to powerful indie rock infused with alt-country grit. A commanding vocalist, Ray is a community-minded dreamer whose shows blur the line between performance and gathering—blending humor, tenderness, and a touch of wild queer magic.

Learn more about Maggie Ray HERE.

All ages welcome.

past.title: Tasting: LDT Wine Co.
past.body:
The LDT tale begins in Lake Tahoe with two friends, passionate about chasing down good wine, deep powder, and occasionally trouble.

After one particularly epic blower day, Christopher Stiffler and McIntosh Forrence settled down for a little après that transitioned into a big evening with more beverages. With stoke still high from the day's adventure, they stayed up late to ponder the meaning of life and the future. Fortune favors the bold and they weren't getting any younger. They agreed to follow their shared passion and that it was time to carve out their spot in the wine world.

That late night conversation turned into daytime discussions and serious strategic planning. Stiffler and Forrence determined it was time to leave their beloved Tahoe powder and, in 2014, LDT Wine Co. made their first vintage in the Willamette Valley.

Alas, the two hour drive to Meadows from the Valley was unbearable. In 2016 they jumped at the chance to move to the Columbia River Gorge, finally able to combine their passions for wine and skiing and feel that ol' familiar stoke a bit more often.

Learn more HERE.
